name: umbraco
description:
Umbraco CLI — manage your Umbraco CMS from the terminal.

Quick start:
  umbraco auth login --host https://mysite.com
  umbraco content list --output json
  umbraco content list | jq '.data[].name'

All commands support --output json (default when stdout is piped).
Use UMBRACO_HOST, UMBRACO_CLIENT_ID, UMBRACO_CLIENT_SECRET for CI/CD.

options.name: --host
options.description: Umbraco instance base URL (overrides config / UMBRACO_HOST).

options.name: --token
options.description: Raw bearer token (overrides credential store).

options.name: --output
options.description: Output format: json | human | csv (default: json when piped, human in terminal).

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress success confirmations (e.g. "Deleted."). Requested data, errors, and exit codes are unaffected.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Write the HTTP method, URL, selected headers and status to stderr. Request and response bodies are NOT included - use --dry-run to see the request body.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Preview the HTTP request a write command would send (method, URL, body) without executing it. No effect on read commands.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Skip the confirmation prompt on destructive commands (delete). Required to run a destructive command non-interactively (piped/scripted/agent).

options.name: --readonly
options.description: Block all write operations (create/update/delete/publish) for this session. Can also be set with UMBRACO_READONLY=1.

options.name: --fields
options.description: Comma-separated fields to keep in JSON output (e.g. id,name), in that order. Trims each result to those top-level fields to keep output small.

options.name: --config
options.description: Path to config file (default: C:\Users\jack\AppData\Roaming\Umbraco\config.json).

options.name: --profile
options.description: Named credential profile to use (see 'auth profile list'). Also settable with UMBRACO_PROFILE. Defaults to the configured default profile.

commands.name: auth
commands.description:
Manage authentication with your Umbraco instance.

Examples:
  umbraco auth login --host https://mysite.com --client-id <id> --client-secret <secret>
  umbraco auth whoami
  umbraco auth logout

commands.name: login
commands.description:
Authenticate with an Umbraco instance using Client Credentials.
Credentials are saved to config for future calls.

Examples:
  umbraco auth login
  umbraco auth login --host https://mysite.com --client-id <id> --client-secret <secret>
  umbraco auth login --output json --host https://mysite.com --client-id <id> --client-secret <secret>

options.name: --client-id
options.description: OAuth2 Client ID from the Umbraco API Users section.

options.name: --client-secret
options.description: OAuth2 Client Secret from the Umbraco API Users section.

commands.name: logout
commands.description:
Remove stored Umbraco credentials for a profile.

The default profile is used unless --profile is given.

Examples:
  umbraco auth logout
  umbraco auth logout --profile prod

commands.name: profile
commands.description:
List saved credential profiles and choose the default.

Examples:
  umbraco auth profile list
  umbraco auth profile use prod

commands.name: list
commands.description:
List saved credential profiles and which one is the default.

Examples:
  umbraco auth profile list
  umbraco auth profile list --output json

commands.name: use
commands.description:
Set the default credential profile.

Examples:
  umbraco auth profile use prod
  umbraco auth profile use default

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: The profile to make the default.

commands.name: whoami
commands.description:
Show the currently authenticated backoffice user and instance details.

Examples:
  umbraco auth whoami
  umbraco auth whoami --output json

commands.name: doctor
commands.description:
Diagnose connectivity, TLS, credentials, authentication and instance version.

Examples:
  umbraco auth doctor
  umbraco auth doctor --output json

commands.name: content
commands.description:
Manage Umbraco content items (create, read, update, delete, publish).

Examples:
  umbraco content list --output json
  umbraco content get <id>
  umbraco content create --document-type textPage --name "My Page"
  umbraco content publish <id>

commands.name: list
commands.description:
List content items at the root, or the children of a parent.

Returns a paginated list of top-level or child content nodes.

Examples:
  umbraco content list
  umbraco content list --parent <id> --take 50
  umbraco content list --output json | jq '.data[].name'

options.name: --parent
options.description: Parent content item id; lists root items if omitted.

options.name: --skip
options.description: Number of items to skip, for paging (default 0).

options.name: --take
options.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 100). meta.hasMore says whether there are more.

commands.name: tree
commands.description:
Walk the content tree into a flat list of nodes.

Each node carries its depth and parent id.

Examples:
  umbraco content tree                       # direct children of the root
  umbraco content tree --parent <id> --recursive
  umbraco content tree --depth 3 --output json

options.name: --parent
options.description: Node whose subtree to walk. Walks from the content root if omitted.

options.name: --recursive
options.description: Descend all levels, up to a safety cap of 50. Without it, only direct children are listed.

options.name: --depth
options.description: Maximum levels to descend (1 = direct children, capped at 50). Overrides --recursive when given.

commands.name: find
commands.description:
Locate content by display name (server search) or by a name path from the root.

Examples:
  umbraco content find --name About
  umbraco content find --name Team --parent <section-id>
  umbraco content find --path "Home/About/Team"

options.name: --skip
options.description: Number of items to skip, for paging (default 0).

options.name: --take
options.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 100). meta.hasMore says whether there are more.

options.name: --name
options.description: Text to match against the display name (contains, case-insensitive).

options.name: --path
options.description: A /-separated path of node names from the root, e.g. "Home/About".

options.name: --parent
options.description: With --name, scope the search to this node's subtree.

commands.name: get
commands.description:
Get a content item by id, including all property values.

Examples:
  umbraco content get 3f7a8b2e-1234-5678-abcd-ef0123456789
  umbraco content get <id> -o json | jq .data.values

commands.name: create
commands.description:
Create a new content item. Supply --json-body for full property control.

Examples:
  umbraco content create --document-type textPage --name "About"
  umbraco content create --document-type textPage --name "Child" --parent <id>
  umbraco content create --document-type blogPost --name "Post" --culture da-DK
  umbraco content create --json-body ./body.json

options.name: --document-type
options.description: Alias of the document type to create (e.g. textPage, blogPost). Required unless --json-body or --schema is used.

options.name: --name
options.description: Display name for the new content item. Required unless --json-body or --schema is used.

options.name: --parent
options.description: Parent content item id. Omit to create at the root.

options.name: --id
options.description: Optional client-supplied id, so a retried create is idempotent.

options.name: --culture
options.description: Culture of the name (e.g. en-US). Omitted, a type that varies by culture gets the default language and an invariant type gets none.

options.name: --template
options.description: Template for the new item, by alias or id. Omitted, the document type's default is used.

options.name: --json-body
options.description: Path to a JSON file (or - for stdin) containing the full create request body. --id and --template still apply; the other field flags go in the body instead.

options.name: --schema
options.description: Print the JSON Schema of the --json-body request and exit (no host needed).

commands.name: update
commands.description:
Update an existing content item from a JSON body file.

Values and variants in the body are MERGED into the item, matched on alias + culture + segment: anything you leave out keeps its current value, and the item's template is preserved. Pass --replace for the old behaviour, where the body's values and variants replace the item's wholesale.

Examples:
  umbraco content update 3f7a8b2e-... --json-body ./update.json
  umbraco content update 3f7a8b2e-... --json-body ./full.json --replace
  umbraco content update 3f7a8b2e-... --json-body ./update.json --template blogPost
  umbraco content update 3f7a8b2e-... --template blogPost

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: Content item ID. Required unless --schema is used.

options.name: --replace
options.description: Replace the item's values and variants with the body's instead of merging into them. Anything absent from the body is cleared.

options.name: --template
options.description: Template to set on the item, by alias or id. Omitted, the current template is kept.

options.name: --json-body
options.description: Path to a JSON file (or - for stdin) containing the update request body. Required unless --schema is used.

options.name: --schema
options.description: Print the JSON Schema of the --json-body request and exit (no host needed).

commands.name: delete
commands.description:
Delete a content item permanently, by id. This cannot be undone.

Examples:
  umbraco content delete 3f7a8b2e-1234-5678-abcd-ef0123456789
  umbraco content delete <id> --yes

commands.name: publish
commands.description:
Publish a content item, making it live. Optionally target specific cultures.

Examples:
  umbraco content publish 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco content publish 3f7a8b2e-... --culture en-US da-DK

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture codes to publish (e.g. en-US da-DK). Publishes all cultures if omitted. Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

options.name: --publish-at
options.description: Schedule the publish for a future time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-01-01T09:00:00Z). Publishes now if omitted.

options.name: --unpublish-at
options.description: Schedule an automatic unpublish at a future time (ISO 8601). Stays published if omitted.

commands.name: domain
commands.description: Read and set a document's Culture and Hostnames bindings.

commands.name: get
commands.description:
Get a document's domains.

Examples:
  umbraco content domain get 3f7a8b2e-...

commands.name: set
commands.description:
Set a document's domains.

The API replaces the whole set, so --domain adds to what is already there rather than replacing it; pass --replace to set exactly what you name and drop the rest.

Examples:
  umbraco content domain set <id> --default-culture en-US --domain example.com=en-US --domain example.com/da=da-DK
  umbraco content domain set <id> --replace --domain example.com=en-US

options.name: --default-culture
options.description: ISO code served when no domain matches. Omit to leave the current default alone.

options.name: --domain
options.description: A binding as host=isoCode, e.g. example.com/da=da-DK. Repeatable.

options.name: --replace
options.description: Set exactly the domains given, removing any others. Without it they are merged in.

commands.name: unpublish
commands.description:
Unpublish a content item, taking it offline.

Optionally target specific cultures.

Examples:
  umbraco content unpublish 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco content unpublish 3f7a8b2e-... --culture en-US

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture codes to unpublish. Unpublishes all cultures if omitted. Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

commands.name: version
commands.description:
List, inspect and roll back a content item's versions.

Examples:
  umbraco content version list <id>
  umbraco content version get <version-id>
  umbraco content version rollback <version-id>

commands.name: list
commands.description:
List the version history of a content item.

A culture-variant item is listed across all its cultures, each row tagged with its culture, unless --culture is given.

Examples:
  umbraco content version list 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco content version list 3f7a8b2e-... --culture en-US

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture code to list versions for (e.g. en-US). Lists every culture if omitted.

options.name: --skip
options.description: Number of items to skip, for paging (default 0).

options.name: --take
options.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 100). meta.hasMore says whether there are more.

commands.name: get
commands.description:
Get one version of a content item, with its values.

Take the id from 'content version list'.

Examples:
  umbraco content version get 7c1d9e4a-...

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: The version's id, from 'content version list'.

commands.name: rollback
commands.description:
Roll a content item back to a previous version.

The ID is a version ID from 'content version list', not the content ID.

Examples:
  umbraco content version rollback 7a1c2d3e-...
  umbraco content version rollback 7a1c2d3e-... --culture en-US

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: Version ID to roll back to (see 'content version list').

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture code to roll back (e.g. en-US).

commands.name: trash
commands.description:
Move a content item to the recycle bin (reversible with 'content restore').

Examples:
  umbraco content trash 3f7a8b2e-...

commands.name: restore
commands.description:
Restore a content item from the recycle bin.

Examples:
  umbraco content restore 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco content restore 3f7a8b2e-... --parent 1a2b3c4d-...
  umbraco content restore 3f7a8b2e-... --to-root

options.name: --parent
options.description: Parent to restore under. Restores to the original parent if omitted.

options.name: --to-root
options.description: Restore to the content root instead of the original parent.

commands.name: empty-recycle-bin
commands.description:
Permanently delete all content items in the recycle bin.

Examples:
  umbraco content empty-recycle-bin --yes

commands.name: move
commands.description:
Move a content item under a new parent.

Examples:
  umbraco content move 3f7a8b2e-... --parent 1a2b3c4d-...
  umbraco content move 3f7a8b2e-...   # to the content root

options.name: --parent
options.description: Target parent ID. Moves to the content root if omitted.

commands.name: sort
commands.description:
Sort a parent's child content items, in the order given or by a field.

With --order the first id goes to the top.

Examples:
  umbraco content sort --parent 1a2b3c4d-... --order 3f7a...,9c4d...,2e6f...
  umbraco content sort --parent 1a2b3c4d-... --by publishDate --desc   # newest first
  umbraco content sort --by name   # the content root, A to Z

options.name: --parent
options.description: Parent ID whose children to reorder. Reorders the content root if omitted.

options.name: --order
options.description: Child content ids in the desired order (first gets sort order 0). Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

options.name: --by
options.description: Order every child by a field instead of listing them: name, createDate, updateDate, publishDate.

options.name: --desc
options.description: With --by, order descending (newest first).

commands.name: copy
commands.description:
Copy a content item under a new parent.

Examples:
  umbraco content copy 3f7a8b2e-... --parent 1a2b3c4d-...
  umbraco content copy 3f7a8b2e-... --include-descendants

options.name: --parent
options.description: Target parent ID. Copies to the content root if omitted.

options.name: --include-descendants
options.description: Also copy the item's descendants.

options.name: --relate
options.description: Create a relation from the copy back to the original.

commands.name: publish-descendants
commands.description:
Publish a content item and its descendants.

Examples:
  umbraco content publish-descendants 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco content publish-descendants 3f7a8b2e-... --include-unpublished --culture en-US

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture codes to publish. Publishes all cultures if omitted. Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

options.name: --include-unpublished
options.description: Also publish descendants that have never been published.

options.name: --wait
options.description: Poll the background publish task until it completes, rather than returning as soon as it is queued.

commands.name: bulk
commands.description:
Run an operation over many content ids read from stdin or a file.

Each id gets its own result.

Examples:
  umbraco content list --fields id | umbraco content bulk publish
  umbraco content bulk delete --file ids.txt --yes

commands.name: delete
commands.description:
Delete many content items permanently, by id (ids from --file or stdin).

Examples:
  umbraco content bulk delete --file ids.txt --yes
  cat ids.txt | umbraco content bulk delete --yes

options.name: --file
options.description: File of ids (one per line). Reads stdin when omitted.

commands.name: publish
commands.description:
Publish many content items by id (ids from --file or stdin).

Examples:
  umbraco content list --fields id | umbraco content bulk publish
  umbraco content bulk publish --file ids.txt --culture en-US

options.name: --file
options.description: File of ids (one per line). Reads stdin when omitted.

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture codes to publish. Publishes all cultures if omitted. Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

commands.name: unpublish
commands.description:
Unpublish many content items by id (ids from --file or stdin).

Examples:
  umbraco content bulk unpublish --file ids.txt
  umbraco content bulk unpublish --file ids.txt --culture da-DK

options.name: --file
options.description: File of ids (one per line). Reads stdin when omitted.

options.name: --culture
options.description: ISO culture codes to unpublish. Unpublishes all cultures if omitted. Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

commands.name: export
commands.description:
Export a content subtree to a portable JSON snapshot.

Examples:
  umbraco content export --out content.json
  umbraco content export --root 3f7a8b2e-... --out subtree.json
  umbraco content export | jq '.data.documents | length'

options.name: --root
options.description: Export only this document's subtree (root included). Omit for the whole tree.

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the snapshot to this file (bare JSON, no envelope). Omit to write the snapshot to stdout inside the success envelope.

commands.name: diff
commands.description:
Compare a content snapshot against the live instance (read-only).

Examples:
  umbraco content diff content.json
  umbraco content export | umbraco content diff -

arguments.name: snapshot
arguments.description: Path to a snapshot file produced by 'content export', or '-' for stdin.

commands.name: apply
commands.description:
Apply a content snapshot to the live instance.

Creates, updates and sets publish state; --prune also deletes.

Examples:
  umbraco content apply content.json --dry-run
  umbraco content apply content.json
  umbraco content apply content.json --no-state
  umbraco content apply content.json --prune --yes
  umbraco content apply content.json --prune --exclude-type contactSubmission --yes

A whole-tree prune also deletes whatever was created on the target since the export - form submissions, editors' drafts. Export with --root to prune one subtree, or leave content alone with --exclude-type / --exclude-root.

Publish state is applied too: cultures published in the snapshot are published, and live cultures the snapshot has unpublished are unpublished.

arguments.name: snapshot
arguments.description: Path to a snapshot file produced by 'content export', or '-' for stdin.

options.name: --prune
options.description: Also DELETE live documents (within the snapshot's scope) that the snapshot does not contain. Destructive: requires --yes when non-interactive.

options.name: --no-state
options.description: Do not publish or unpublish: new documents stay drafts and live publish state is left as it is.

options.name: --exclude-type
options.description: With --prune, never delete documents of this document type (alias or id). Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

options.name: --exclude-root
options.description: With --prune, never delete this document or anything under it (id). Repeat the option, or separate values with commas.

commands.name: media
commands.description:
Manage Umbraco media library items (upload, list, get, delete).

Examples:
  umbraco media list
  umbraco media upload ./photo.jpg --parent <folder-id>
  umbraco media delete <id>

commands.name: list
commands.description:
List media items in the media library.

Examples:
  umbraco media list
  umbraco media list --parent <folder-id> --output json

options.name: --parent
options.description: Parent media folder id; lists root media items if omitted.

options.name: --skip
options.description: Number of items to skip, for paging (default 0).

options.name: --take
options.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 100). meta.hasMore says whether there are more.

commands.name: tree
commands.description:
Walk the media tree into a flat list of nodes.

Each node carries its depth and parent id.

Examples:
  umbraco media tree                       # direct children of the root
  umbraco media tree --parent <folder-id> --recursive
  umbraco media tree --depth 3 --output json

options.name: --parent
options.description: Folder whose subtree to walk. Walks from the media root if omitted.

options.name: --recursive
options.description: Descend all levels, up to a safety cap of 50. Without it, only direct children are listed.

options.name: --depth
options.description: Maximum levels to descend (1 = direct children, capped at 50). Overrides --recursive when given.

commands.name: find
commands.description:
Locate media by display name (server search) or by a name path from the root.

Examples:
  umbraco media find --name logo
  umbraco media find --name hero --parent <folder-id>
  umbraco media find --path "Images/Logos/Primary"

options.name: --skip
options.description: Number of items to skip, for paging (default 0).

options.name: --take
options.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 100). meta.hasMore says whether there are more.

options.name: --name
options.description: Text to match against the display name (contains, case-insensitive).

options.name: --path
options.description: A /-separated path of node names from the root, e.g. "Images/Logos".

options.name: --parent
options.description: With --name, scope the search to this folder's subtree.

commands.name: get
commands.description:
Get a media item by id, including its public URL and file metadata.

Width, height, size and extension come back under 'values', keyed by the aliases Umbraco uses (umbracoWidth, umbracoHeight, umbracoBytes, umbracoExtension); the URL comes back under 'urls', one entry per culture.

Examples:
  umbraco media get 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco media get <id> -o json | jq .data.urls

commands.name: upload
commands.description:
Upload a local file as a media item (staged via temporary-file for large files).

Examples:
  umbraco media upload ./logo.png
  umbraco media upload ./big-video.mp4 --media-type File --name "Promo"
  umbraco media upload ./photo.jpg --parent 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco media upload ./report.pdf --media-type brochure --id 3f7a8b2e-... --value title="Annual report"

options.name: --parent
options.description: Id of the media folder to upload into. Omit for the media root.

options.name: --name
options.description: Display name for the media item. Defaults to the filename.

options.name: --media-type
options.description: Media type to create the item as: a media type id, alias or name (e.g. image, Image, File). Defaults to Image.

options.name: --id
options.description: Id to create the item with, so it keeps the same id on every instance (content references media by id). Omit to generate one.

options.name: --value
options.description: Property values as alias=value, e.g. title="Annual report". Repeatable. Needed for a media type with required fields.

commands.name: update
commands.description:
Update a media item's property values and name.

They are MERGED into the item, matched on alias + culture + segment: anything you leave out, the uploaded file included, keeps its current value. --replace sends the body's values and variants as the whole set.

Examples:
  umbraco media update 3f7a8b2e-... --value summary="Forms for new members" --value pageCount=4
  umbraco media update 3f7a8b2e-... --name "Membership forms"
  umbraco media update 3f7a8b2e-... --json-body ./media.json

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: Media item ID. Required unless --schema is used.

options.name: --name
options.description: New display name.

options.name: --value
options.description: Property values as alias=value, e.g. summary="...". Repeatable.

options.name: --replace
options.description: Replace the item's values and variants with the body's instead of merging into them. Anything absent from the body is cleared - the uploaded file included.

options.name: --json-body
options.description: Path to a JSON file (or - for stdin) with values and variants to merge; --name and --value are applied on top of it.

options.name: --schema
options.description: Print the JSON Schema of the --json-body request and exit (no host needed).

commands.name: folder
commands.description: Create media folders to organise uploads.

commands.name: create
commands.description:
Create a media folder.

A folder is an ordinary media item of the Folder media type, so it is deleted, moved and trashed with the usual media verbs.

Examples:
  umbraco media folder create --name Blog
  umbraco media folder create --name 2026 --parent 3f7a8b2e-...

options.name: --name
options.description: Folder name.

options.name: --parent
options.description: Parent folder id. Creates at the media root when omitted.

options.name: --id
options.description: Optional client-supplied id, so a retried create is idempotent.

commands.name: delete
commands.description:
Delete a media item permanently, by id.

Examples:
  umbraco media delete 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco media delete <id> --yes

commands.name: trash
commands.description:
Move a media item to the recycle bin (reversible with 'media restore').

Examples:
  umbraco media trash 3f7a8b2e-...

commands.name: restore
commands.description:
Restore a media item from the recycle bin.

Examples:
  umbraco media restore 3f7a8b2e-...
  umbraco media restore 3f7a8b2e-... --parent 1a2b3c4d-...
  umbraco media restore 3f7a8b2e-... --to-root

options.name: --parent
options.description: Folder to restore under. Restores to the original parent if omitted.

options.name: --to-root
options.description: Restore to the media root instead of the original parent.

commands.name: empty-recycle-bin
commands.description:
Permanently delete all media items in the recycle bin.

Examples:
  umbraco media empty-recycle-bin --yes

commands.name: move
commands.description:
Move a media item under a new parent folder.

Examples:
  umbraco media move 3f7a8b2e-... --parent 1a2b3c4d-...
  umbraco media move 3f7a8b2e-...   # to the media root

options.name: --parent
options.description: Target folder ID. Moves to the media root if omitted.

commands.name: sort
commands.description:
Sort a folder's child media items, in the order given or by a field.
